Definition: from ἔλεφας (an "elephant"); elephantine, i.e. (by implication) composed of ivory:--of ivory.
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, elephántinos is the word for of ivory. In Revelation 18:12, the text says "and all manner vessels of ivory."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, elephántinos means of ivory, and I leave it at that.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
